  2. WHAT IS SWOT ANALYSIS? 
SWOT Analysis is a tool used for strategic planning and strategic management in organizations. It 
can be used effectively to build organizational strategy and competitive strategy. In accordance with the 
System Approach, organizations are wholes that are in interaction with their environments and consist of 
various sub-systems. In this s

Four-row definition table. Organizational Strengths: characteristics that give advantage over others in the industry. Organizational Weaknesses: characteristics that place the organisation at a disadvantage relative to others. Environmental Opportunities: external elements that give benefits for the organization. Environmental Threats: external elements that could cause trouble for it.

Checklist table in two parts. The first lists candidate internal factors in four columns — among them advertising, brand names, channel management, company reputation, costs, customer loyalty, distribution, economies of scale, financial resources, human resources, leadership, management, market share, organizational structure, product/service quality, purchasing, quality control, research and development, selling and technology. The second lists the sources of external factors: economic, political-legal, social, technological and industry forces.

The paper's worked example: a completed four-quadrant SWOT matrix for an international sportswear brand (Nike). Strengths include global brand recognition, reputation for quality, a lean contract-manufacturing model, R&D, Fortune 500 standing and innovative marketing. Weaknesses include income dependence on footwear, retail price sensitivity, past non-disclosure about partner companies, and labour-practice allegations. Opportunities include fashion-driven replacement demand, product extension into sportswear, sunglasses and jewellery, and emerging markets. Threats include currency exposure, a highly competitive market, price-comparison behaviour and environmental/recession pressure.

The TOWS matrix: strengths and weaknesses across the top, opportunities and threats down the side, each cell naming the strategy that pairing implies. SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the organization's strengths. WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities. ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats. WT — prevent weaknesses to avoid making the organization more susceptible to threats. This is the step that turns the four lists into strategy.

6. DISADVANTAGES AND LIMITATIONS OF SWOT ANALYSIS  
SWOT Analysis is one of the most widely used technique of the strategic management process. The 
criticism is directed to SWOT Analysis in spite of its wide use as an analysis tool. In this regard, the 
criticisms include that it is not effective enough as a part of organizational strategy, it cannot go beyond 
making a definition regarding the current situation
